protocol.py: 4 biology problems (3 warnings, 1 note).

1. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: A mix stroke as big as the well, 6 wells: 25 ul in 25 ul
   line 48:  p300.transfer(25, tuberack["A2"], tuberack[well], mix_after=(3, 25))
   At line 48 the tip mixes tubes A3, A4, A5, A6, B1 and B2 in slot 2 with 3 strokes of 25
   ul in a well holding 25 ul (this line did it 6 times). A stroke of the whole well draws
   air at the bottom and foams the liquid. Integra draws over 80% of the well five times;
   three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the
   concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits the
   error.
   Affected: tubes A3, A4, A5, A6, B1 and B2 in slot 2.
   Fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (20 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 20,
   well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [9365b6f1b8c0]

2. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: A pipette too small to mix 7 wells: 300 ul at most in 50 to 1525 ul
   line 50:  p300.transfer(25, tuberack[prev_well], tuberack[well], mix_after=(3, 25))
   At line 50 the tip mixes tubes A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1 and B2 in slot 2 with 3 strokes of
   25 ul in a well holding 50 to 1525 ul (this line did it 7 times). The P300 can draw at
   most 300 ul, under a fifth of the well: no stroke it can make will mix this well, however
   many times. 3 strokes of 25 ul move 0.25 to 1.5 of the pipette's 300 ul in all; it takes
   about 2 pipette-fulls of strokes to mix (the mixing work). Integra draws over 80% of the
   well five times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is
   not at the concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every later step
   inherits the error.
   Affected: tubes A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1 and B2 in slot 2.
   Fix: Mix with a bigger pipette (a P1000 for this well): at least 5 strokes of 1000 ul,
   `mix(5, 1000, well)`.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [522320231ae2]

3. WARNING WELL-CAPACITY: More liquid than the well is rated for: 1525 ul against 1500 ul, 1
well
   line 50:  p300.transfer(25, tuberack[prev_well], tuberack[well], mix_after=(3, 25))
   At line 50 the robot filled tube A2 in slot 2 past the 1500 ul the maker states for it,
   reaching 1525 ul, under the 1898 ul the well holds to its rim. Above the stated maximum
   the liquid climbs the wall and wets the seal, a tip going in displaces it over the edge,
   and the volumes still add up on paper, so the plate map does not see it and the simulator
   says nothing. Wells: tube A2 in slot 2.
   Affected: tube A2 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use labware rated for the volume, or scale every volume down so the fullest well
   stays under the stated maximum with room to mix.
   Source: Opentrons labware schema 2: totalLiquidVolume, the total well volume in
   microlitres
           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json
   Source: Bartley et al. 2023, LabOP: a protocol never adds more liquid than its container
   holds
           https://jakebeal.github.io/Publications/JETC23-LabOP.pdf
   [39ce5d399ef7]

4. NOTE WELL-CAPACITY: Declared more than the well holds: 20000 ul in a 15015 ul well, 1
well
   line 85:  p300.transfer(200, reservoir["A1"], dst_plate[well])
   At line 85 the robot draws from well A1 in slot 5, which the protocol declares (line 32)
   to hold 20000 ul; the well holds 15014.5 ul. The prep sheet cannot be followed as
   written. Wells: well A1 in slot 5.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 5.
   Fix: Declare what the well can really hold, or use a bigger container.
   Source: Opentrons labware schema 2: totalLiquidVolume, the total well volume in
   microlitres
           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json
   Source: Bartley et al. 2023, LabOP: a protocol never adds more liquid than its container
   holds
           https://jakebeal.github.io/Publications/JETC23-LabOP.pdf
   [5ef7f3e50933]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
